exact_call_totals.method: Counts derived from all raw/captured tool-call inputs, manually expanding t02 four-command loop and counting Promise.allSettled elements. These counts match the 62 unique host events and unique invocation IDs. All 62 captured events exactly match the original host-events.json after the documented bootstrap-path redaction. No dynamic or direct aide calls appear in inputs; all nested calls are exec_command or apply_patch.

runtime_accounting.method: Read only exact log paths from logs.json. Selected session_meta identity/provider/CLI fields, turn_context model/effort fields, token_usage_record counters, task_complete timing, and tool call/output records; did not expose reasoning or base instructions. Compared raw tool inputs and all decoded measurement records to captures. Independently summed unique response IDs, compared each sum to final cumulative counters and published summaries, and verified session/actor identity and duration.
runtime_accounting.counter_interpretation: Cached input is a subset of input, and reasoning output is a subset of output. Runtime total equals input plus output; do not add cached/reasoning counters again. These are runtime reports, not billing or provider-token savings. No missing counter or cumulative mismatch found.

accounting_concerns_and_corrections.finding: payload_bytes measures extracted tool text at the host_result hook boundary, before later orchestration output truncation/rendering. It does not establish exact source bytes delivered in the final model context. Inner tool formatting or truncation may already have occurred.
accounting_concerns_and_corrections.correction: Label host_byte_groups as hook-boundary text bytes and runtime_tool_result_text_bytes as logged tool-result text including protocol/rendering wrappers. Do not treat their difference as token savings or exclusively wrapper overhead.

accounting_concerns_and_corrections.finding: t02 has 14 host events but only 10 decoded bodies. Its fourth exec result contains an explicit outer truncation warning and combined partially truncated JSON text, so the collector cannot decode the four nested source results. Those four host results total 39,428 bytes. The decoded subtotal 23,012 is accurate for the bodies decoded, not a complete source-output total.
accounting_concerns_and_corrections.correction: Retain decoded_body_count=10, label decoded_body_bytes=23012 as a partial subtotal, and keep exact complete post-orchestration source-body bytes unknown/null. Do not reconstruct complete delivery from host bytes. t01 has no actual truncation warning; the word Truncated appears only in source comments.

accounting_concerns_and_corrections.finding: t05 and t06 each have one 213-byte native Edit host event whose outer runtime tool-result text is {}. The shell/MCP body decoder does not extract that edit result. Thus t05 has 6 decoded bodies totaling 5,488 versus 7 host events totaling 5,701, and t06 has 7 totaling 3,086 versus 8 totaling 3,299.
accounting_concerns_and_corrections.correction: Keep the missing edit-body coverage explicit. A failed host_and_decoded_totals_match flag here indicates different measurement surfaces and decoder coverage, not an omitted tool call or zero host output.

accounting_concerns_and_corrections.finding: retrieval_output includes file listings, source searches, README/provided-test reads and source code reads, sometimes within one command. It is exploration-result text, not exclusively source-file contents.
accounting_concerns_and_corrections.correction: Use the existing category as a broad retrieval/exploration output metric; do not imply a separately measured source-only byte total.

accounting_concerns_and_corrections.finding: Assisted treatment permits but does not require aide tools. All three assisted trials and all three ordinary trials used zero aide retrieval calls, verified from complete raw tool-call inputs as well as host events.
accounting_concerns_and_corrections.correction: Do not attribute any pairwise difference to aide retrieval use or infer retrieval savings. Report this fixed six-trial sample descriptively as optional-availability outcomes; no causal generalization.

t05.reason: Adds a Bash output-envelope branch, validates non-array payload/metadata and safe integer exit, rejects defined alternate representations and isImage:true, returns a new spread object replacing only output. Known empty text works. Legacy Bash and MCP branches otherwise remain intact.

t06.reason: Same behavior as t05 for supported ordinary adapter payloads. The explicit typeof metadata.exit number check is redundant with Number.isSafeInteger and does not change semantics.

edit_patch_review.shared_boundary_note: Both select the new branch when output is defined, so malformed or mixed defined-output envelopes are rejected rather than falling back to legacy streams. That matches the task. With output undefined, legacy stream envelopes remain supported. No source or frozen tests were edited by the reviewer.
